complexity.notes: Each element enters the set once and is removed once, so the work is O(1) amortized per element; the algorithm meets the required O(n) average time. Worst case degrades to O(n^2) only under adversarially colliding integer hashes, which the generalized problem permits but the stated +-10^9 range makes practically unreachable. Code is clean and readable.
complexity.summary: Builds a set of the values, then repeatedly pops an element and expands outward in both directions, removing each run's members from the set as they are consumed so every value is processed once. The maximum run length seen is returned.
